context:
Goal: a PR whose own changes did not move keeps its review, so the merge queue does not stall.
Problem (rule): a ruling covers only the act it names. Yours names a clean merge of main, and the empty commit is a reading of it.
Based on (read): your Nov 10 14:07 CST ruling: "a review log survives a clean main merge"; any other difference keeps today's rules.
Based on (read): incident #2562: an empty commit on a reviewed head made its review read stale.
Based on (measured): round 2 (reviewer sonnet, 14:26 CST) found no way for an empty commit to change the lane's diff.
Departs from: main, where an empty commit after review makes the log stale — adds the empty commit to the pushes the log survives.
Meanwhile: #2563's test fix goes on; its merge waits on this answer.
holds: Whether a commit that changes no file, pushed after review, keeps the PR's review log.

options.gain: A push that changes nothing never costs a fresh review.
options.how: An empty commit keeps the review log, as #2563 builds it.
options.label: Keep it (Recommended)
options.lose: One more case the merge tool must prove.

options.gain: The rule stays exactly as you said it.
options.how: #2563 removes the empty-commit case. An empty commit makes the log stale, as today.
options.label: Drop it
options.lose: An empty commit costs a fix check, as in incident #2562.

title: Should an empty commit after review keep the review log valid?
why: Your Nov 10 14:07 ruling covers a clean merge of main only. #2563 also keeps the review log after an empty commit, on the coordinator's reading.
